## package loading & import dataset
Loading relevant packages for analysis, plots and comfortable analysis
Color setting for the visualization conditions
```{r}
# packages / imports
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
library(psych)
library(readxl)
library(ez)

library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)
library(ggpubr)
library(rstatix)

## RGBD, PC = Point cloud, OT = open television

colors_iam <- c(
    "RGBs"= "#1F77B4",     # blue
    "OT"= "#FF7F0E",       # orange
    "PC"= "#2CA02C",       # green
    "PC+RGB"= "#D62728",   # red
    "PC_RGB" = "#D62728"
)

```



Import of the .xlxs raw dataset => Loading Dataset
```{r}

rawDataAN <- read_excel("rawDataAN.xlsx")
View(rawDataAN)
```

```{r}

data <- rawDataAN

# remove []
colnames(data) <- gsub("\\[|\\]", "", colnames(data)) 

```



Import data set
```{r}
rawDataANBinaryPerformance <- read_excel("rawDataANBinaryPerformance.xlsx")
View(rawDataANBinaryPerformance)
```

```{r}
dataPer <- rawDataANBinaryPerformance
dim(dataPer)

colnames(dataPer) <- gsub("\\[|\\]", "", colnames(dataPer)) 
```

# Prior experience
Self reported prior experience in VR, Gaming and especially in simulator games - analysed as individual items
Question:
"Please tell us your prior experience with gaming and VR by answering the following questions."
Answer format for frequencies:
1 - never, 2 - less than 1x per month, 3 - 1x per month, 4 - 2-3x per month
5 - 1x per week, 6 - 2-3x per week, 7 - daily

Analysis: Likert scale, interpreted as orderd (not equal distances)

Adding labels to the 3 variables (L in the end of the variable name is used to illustrate that)
```{r}
# adding labels
data$experienceVRL <- ordered(data$priorExperienceVR,
  levels = c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7),
  labels = c("never", "less than 1x per month", "1x per month", "2-3x per month",
             "1x per week", "2-3x per week", "daily"))


data$experienceGameL <- ordered(data$priorExperienceGame,
  levels = c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7),
  labels = c("never", "less than 1x per month", "1x per month", "2-3x per month",
             "1x per week", "2-3x per week", "daily"))

data$experienceSimL <- ordered(data$priorExperienceGsim,
  levels = c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7),
  labels = c("never", "less than 1x per month", "1x per month", "2-3x per month",
             "1x per week", "2-3x per week", "daily"))

```


Item VR: "Do you already have experience with VR? For example, in another experiment or in VR gaming?"
```{r}
data %>%
  group_by(experienceVRL) %>%
  summarise(n = n()) %>%
  mutate(freq = n / sum(n))
```

# Individual traits or tendencies
Evaluation of ATI (affinity for technology interaction) and immersive tendency


## ATI evaluation

Scale information for participants:
"In the following questionnaire, we will ask you about your interaction with technical systems. The term “technical systems” refers to apps and other software applications, as well as entire digital devices (e.g., mobile phone, computer, TV, car navigation). Please indicate the degree to which you agree/disagree with the following statements."

Answer format: 1 - 6; completely disagree, largely disagree, slightly disagree, slightly agree, largely agree, completely agree


1. renaming columns - indication of items that need to be reversed (i3, i6, i8)
```{r}
# rename column names
data <- data %>%
  rename(
    # situation 1
    ATI1 = ATIATI1,
    ATI2 = ATIATI2,
    ATI3r = ATIATI3,
    ATI4 = ATIATI4,
    ATI5 = ATIATI5,
    ATI6r = ATIATI6,
    ATI7 = ATIATI7,
    ATI8r = ATIATI8,
    ATI9 = ATIATI9,
  )
```

2. recoding of the 3 items, save as new variables
```{r}
data <- data %>%
  mutate(
    ATI3 = recode(ATI3r, `6` = 1, `5` = 2, `4` = 3, `3` = 4, `2` = 5, `1` = 6),
    ATI6 = recode(ATI6r, `6` = 1, `5` = 2, `4` = 3, `3` = 4, `2` = 5, `1` = 6),
    ATI8 = recode(ATI8r, `6` = 1, `5` = 2, `4` = 3, `3` = 4, `2` = 5, `1` = 6)
  )

```

3. check internal consistency (reliability of the scale) - cronbachs alpha 

https://bjoernwalther.com/cronbachs-alpha-in-r-berechnen/

detailed analysis:
```{r}
alpha(data[, c("ATI1", "ATI2", "ATI3", "ATI4", "ATI5", "ATI6",  
               "ATI7",  "ATI8",  "ATI9")], check.keys =TRUE)
```

single value:
```{r}
alpha(data[, c("ATI1", "ATI2", "ATI3", "ATI4", "ATI5", "ATI6",  
               "ATI7",  "ATI8",  "ATI9")])$total$raw_alpha
```

4. rowwise mean to generate the ATI scor for each participant 
Result of 3. should be >0.65 / > 0.7
```{r}
data <- data %>%
  mutate(ATI = rowMeans(select(., ATI1, ATI2, ATI3, ATI4, ATI5, ATI6, 
                                          ATI7, ATI8, ATI9, ), na.rm = TRUE))
```


5. descriptive analysis of ATI scores
```{r}
describe(data$ATI)
```

6. Visual illustration with a boxplot
Notch for internal distribution illustration; could be deleted for more classical illustration
```{r}
boxplot(data$ATI, notch=FALSE,
        main="Affinity for technology interaction",
        xlab="ATI for all participants", 
        ylab="Response means 1 (low) - 6 (high)",
        ylim = c(1, 6))
```

## Immersive tendency evaluation
Subscales: 
Focus: Items 1 + 2 + 3 + 8 + 13
Implication: Items 4 + 5 + 10 + 12 + 18
Emotions: Items 11 + 15 + 16 + 17
Game: items 6 + 9 + 14

Answer scale: 1 - low/never to 7 - high/very often


1. renaming variables (no recoding required)
Caution: the original names come from different pages in limesurvey => renaming for clearer understanding
```{r}
data <- data %>%
  rename(
    it1 = iT1i1, it2 = iT1i2, 
    it3 = iT2i3, 
    it4 = iT3i4, it5 = iT3i5, it6 = iT3i6, 
    it7 = iT4i7,
    it8 = iT5i8, 
    it9 = iT6i9, it10 = iT6i10, it11 = iT6i11, it12 = iT6i12,   
    it13 = iT7i13,
    it14 = iT8i14, it15 = iT8i15, it16 = iT8i16, it17 = iT8i17, it18 = iT8i18,
  )
```


2. internal consistency for the subscales & rowwise mean computation
Focus:
```{r}
alpha(data[, c("it1", "it2", "it3", "it8", "it13")], check.keys =TRUE)
```
c alpha = .4436 => very low

```{r}
data <- data %>%
  mutate(itFocus = rowMeans(select(., it1, it2, it3, it8, it13), na.rm = TRUE))
```


Implication:
```{r}
alpha(data[, c("it4", "it5", "it10", "it12", "it18")], check.keys =TRUE)
```
c alpha: .7076


```{r}
data <- data %>%
  mutate(itImplication = rowMeans(select(., it4, it5, it10, it12, it18), na.rm = TRUE))
```



Emotion:
```{r}
alpha(data[, c("it11", "it15", "it16", "it17")], check.keys =TRUE)
```
c alpha .7065

```{r}
data <- data %>%
  mutate(itEmotion = rowMeans(select(., it11, it15, it16, it17), na.rm = TRUE))
```



Game:
```{r}
alpha(data[, c("it6", "it9", "it14")], check.keys =TRUE)
```
c alpha = .386 => very low


```{r}
data <- data %>%
  mutate(itGame = rowMeans(select(., it6, it9, it14), na.rm = TRUE))
```

Physically fit: item 7


```{r}
#Long format
tlx_long <- data %>%

  select(starts_with("NasaTLX")) %>%

  pivot_longer(
    cols = everything(),
    names_to   = c("Condition", "Dimension"),
    names_pattern = "NasaTLX(\\d+)(.*)",
    values_to  = "Score"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Condition = recode(Condition,
      `1` = "RGBs",
      `2` = "PC",
      `3` = "PC+RGB",
      `4` = "OT"
    ),
    Condition = factor(Condition,
      levels = c("RGBs", "PC", "PC+RGB", "OT")),
    Dimension = recode(Dimension,
      "mD"    = "Mental demand",
      "pD"    = "Physical demand",
      "tD"    = "Temporal demand",
      "per"   = "Performance expectation",
      "effort"= "Effort",
      "frust" = "Frustration"
    ),
    # Reihenfolge der Facetten (optional)
    Dimension = factor(Dimension,
      levels = c("Mental demand", "Physical demand", "Temporal demand",
                 "Performance expectation", "Effort", "Frustration"))
  )
```


```{r}
plot_tlx_dim <- function(dim_name) {
  ggplot(
    tlx_long %>% filter(Dimension == dim_name),
    aes(x = Condition, y = Score, fill = Condition)
  ) +
    geom_boxplot(width = 0.6, outlier.size = 0.7, linewidth = 0.3) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(1, 21), breaks = seq(1, 21, by = 5)) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = colors_iam) +
    labs(
      title = dim_name,
      x = "Condition",                       # jede Kachel eigene Achsen
      y = "Response (1 = low, 21 = high)"
    ) +
    theme_classic(base_size = 9) +
    theme(
      legend.position = "none",
      plot.title      = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5)
    )
}

```

```{r}
p1 <- plot_tlx_dim("Mental demand")
p2 <- plot_tlx_dim("Physical demand")
p3 <- plot_tlx_dim("Temporal demand")
p4 <- plot_tlx_dim("Performance expectation")
p5 <- plot_tlx_dim("Effort")
p6 <- plot_tlx_dim("Frustration")

# 2 Zeilen × 3 Spalten
(p1 | p2 | p3) /
(p4 | p5 | p6)
```

## significance testing NASA

Testing if the differences between conditions are significant in each dimension
Correction within each dimension and an overall correction due to multiple testing

### 0. long format
```{r}
tlx_long <- data %>%
  select(id, starts_with("NasaTLX")) %>%   
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("NasaTLX"),
    names_to   = c("Condition", "Dimension"),
    names_pattern = "NasaTLX(\\d+)(.*)",
    values_to  = "Score"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Condition = recode(Condition,
      `1` = "RGBs",
      `2` = "PC",
      `3` = "PC+RGB",
      `4` = "OT"
    ),
    Condition = factor(Condition, levels = c("RGBs", "PC", "PC+RGB", "OT")),
    Dimension = recode(Dimension,
      "mD"    = "Mental demand",
      "pD"    = "Physical demand",
      "tD"    = "Temporal demand",
      "per"   = "Performance expectation",
      "effort"= "Effort",
      "frust" = "Frustration"
    ),
    Dimension = factor(
      Dimension,
      levels = c("Mental demand", "Physical demand", "Temporal demand",
                 "Performance expectation", "Effort", "Frustration")
    )
  )
```


### 1. Testing if the variances are normally distributed

Mental demand
```{r}
dim_name <- "Mental demand"

mental_data <- tlx_long %>% filter(Dimension == dim_name)

## 2.1 Normalität der Scores pro Condition
mental_data %>%
  group_by(Condition) %>%
  shapiro_test(Score)
# optional: QQ-Plots
ggqqplot(mental_data, "Score", ggtheme = theme_bw()) + facet_wrap(~ Condition)

```


physical demand
```{r}
dim_name <- "Physical demand"

nasa_data <- tlx_long %>% filter(Dimension == dim_name)

## 2.1 Normalität der Scores pro Condition
nasa_data %>%
  group_by(Condition) %>%
  shapiro_test(Score)
# optional: QQ-Plots
ggqqplot(nasa_data, "Score", ggtheme = theme_bw()) + facet_wrap(~ Condition)

```

temporal demand
```{r}
dim_name <- "Temporal demand"

nasa_data <- tlx_long %>% filter(Dimension == dim_name)

## 2.1 Normalität der Scores pro Condition
```

### 2. Testing for any significant differences (including correction)

```{r}
# Friedman tests for all six NASA-TLX dimensions
friedman_results_nasa <- tlx_long %>%
  group_by(Dimension) %>%
  friedman_test(Score ~ Condition | id) %>%   # one Friedman test per Dimension
  ungroup() %>%
  # Holm correction across the six dimensions
  mutate(
    p_holm = p.adjust(p, method = "holm"),
    sig_holm_0.05 = p_holm < 0.05
  )

friedman_results_nasa

```

Description: statistic – Friedman χ²; df – degrees of freedom; p – ungefilterter p-Wert; p_holm – Holm-korrigierter p-Wert (über alle 6 Dimensionen); sig_holm_0.05 – TRUE/FALSE, ob nach Holm noch signifikant bei α = .05


### 3. Post hoc testing for significant differences
```{r}
sig_dims <- friedman_results_nasa %>% # only significant
  filter(sig_holm_0.05 == TRUE) %>%
  pull(Dimension)

posthoc_results_nasa <- tlx_long %>%
  filter(Dimension %in% sig_dims) %>%
  group_by(Dimension) %>%
  pairwise_wilcox_test(
    Score ~ Condition,
    paired = TRUE,
    p.adjust.method = "holm"   # correction WITHIN dimension
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

posthoc_results_nasa
```





```{r}
library(coin)


posthoc_results_nasa_effect <- tlx_long %>%
  filter(Dimension %in% sig_dims) %>%
  group_by(Dimension) %>%
  wilcox_effsize(
    Score ~ Condition,
    paired = TRUE
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

posthoc_results_nasa_effect
```

```{r}

combined_nasa_posthoc <- posthoc_results_nasa %>%
  # join über gemeinsame Spalten
  left_join(
    posthoc_results_nasa_effect,
    by = c(".y.", "group1", "group2", "Dimension", "n1", "n2")
  ) %>%
  # Spalten etwas ordnen/umbenennen
  transmute(
    Dimension,
    Comparison = paste(group1, "vs.", group2),
    n = n1,
    W = statistic,
    p,
    p_adj = p.adj,
    signif = p.adj.signif,
    r = effsize,
    magnitude
  )

combined_nasa_posthoc
```

Creating plot

```{r}
sig_pairs_stars <- posthoc_results_nasa %>%
  filter(p.adj < 0.05) %>%
  transmute(
    Dimension,
    group1,
    group2,
    stars = p.adj.signif   
  )
```



```{r}
library(ggsignif)
plot_tlx_dim <- function(dim_name) {
  data_dim <- tlx_long %>% filter(Dimension == dim_name)
  sig_dim  <- sig_pairs_stars %>% filter(Dimension == dim_name)

  p <- ggplot(data_dim, aes(x = Condition, y = Score, fill = Condition)) +
    geom_boxplot(width = 0.6, outlier.size = 0.7, linewidth = 0.3) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = colors_iam) +
    labs(
      title = dim_name,
      x = "Condition",
      y = "Response (1 = low, 21 = high)"
    ) +
    theme_classic(base_size = 9) +
    theme(
      legend.position = "none",
      plot.title      = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5)
    )

  if (nrow(sig_dim) == 0) {
    return(p + scale_y_continuous(limits = c(1, 21), breaks = seq(1, 21, 5)))
  }

  y_base <- max(data_dim$Score, na.rm = TRUE) + 0.8
  y_step <- 0.8
  sig_dim$y_pos <- y_base + y_step * (seq_len(nrow(sig_dim)) - 1)

  ymax <- max(sig_dim$y_pos) + 0.5

  p +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(1, ymax), breaks = seq(1, 21, 5)) +
    ggsignif::geom_signif(
      data       = sig_dim,
      manual     = TRUE,
      inherit.aes = FALSE,
      aes(
        xmin       = group1,
        xmax       = group2,
        annotations = stars,
        y_position = y_pos
      ),
      tip_length = 0.01,
      textsize   = 3
    )
}
```

### 5. Significance testing

Long format
```{r}
vr_long <- data %>%
  select(
    id,
    RGBs_VRsuq_effectiveness, PC_VRsuq_effectiveness, PC_RGB_VRsuq_effectiveness, OT_VRsuq_effectiveness,
    RGBs_VRsuq_efficiency,    PC_VRsuq_efficiency,    PC_RGB_VRsuq_efficiency,    OT_VRsuq_efficiency,
    RGBs_VRsuq_satisfaction,  PC_VRsuq_satisfaction,  PC_RGB_VRsuq_satisfaction,  OT_VRsuq_satisfaction
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -id,
    names_to = c("Condition", "Dimension"),
    names_pattern = "(.*)_VRsuq_(.*)",
    values_to = "Score"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Condition = factor(Condition,
      levels = c("RGBs", "PC", "PC_RGB", "OT"),
      labels = c("RGBs", "PC", "PC+RGB", "OT")  # für konsistente Labels
    ),
    Dimension = recode(Dimension,
      "effectiveness" = "Effectiveness",
      "efficiency"    = "Efficiency",
      "satisfaction"  = "Satisfaction"
    ),
    Dimension = factor(Dimension,
      levels = c("Effectiveness", "Efficiency", "Satisfaction"))
  )
```


```{r}
library(rstatix)

vr_long %>%
  group_by(Dimension, Condition) %>%
  shapiro_test(Score)
```



```{r}
friedman_vr <- vr_long %>%
  split(.$Dimension) %>%                               # nach Dimension aufteilen
  purrr::map_df(
    ~ rstatix::friedman_test(Score ~ Condition | id,   # Friedman je Teilmenge
                             data = .x),
    .id = "Dimension"                                  # Name aus split als Spalte
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    p_holm = p.adjust(p, method = "holm"),
    sig_holm_0.05 = p_holm < 0.05
  )

friedman_vr
```


### 5. Post hoc tests

```{r}
sig_dims_vr <- friedman_vr %>%
  filter(sig_holm_0.05) %>%
  pull(Dimension)

# Post-hoc Wilcoxon Tests
posthoc_vr <- vr_long %>%
  filter(Dimension %in% sig_dims_vr) %>%
  group_by(Dimension) %>%
  pairwise_wilcox_test(
    Score ~ Condition,
    paired = TRUE,
    p.adjust.method = "holm"
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

posthoc_vr

```



```{r}
posthoc_vr_effect <- vr_long %>%
  filter(Dimension %in% sig_dims_vr) %>%
  group_by(Dimension) %>%
  wilcox_effsize(Score ~ Condition, paired = TRUE) %>%
  ungroup()

posthoc_vr_effect
```

```{r}
combined_vr <- posthoc_vr %>%
  left_join(
    posthoc_vr_effect,
    by = c(".y.", "group1", "group2", "Dimension", "n1", "n2")
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    r = round(effsize, 3)
  ) %>%
  
  transmute(
    Dimension,
    group1,
    group2,
    n = n1,
    W = statistic,
    p,
    p_adj = p.adj,
    signif = p.adj.signif,
    r,
    magnitude
  )

combined_vr
```



Plotting:


Plot function
```{r}
plot_vr_dim <- function(dim_name) {
  
  data_dim <- vr_long %>% filter(Dimension == dim_name)
  sig_dim  <- sig_pairs_vr %>% filter(Dimension == dim_name)
  
  p <- ggplot(
    data_dim,
    aes(x = Condition, y = Score, fill = Condition)
  ) +
    geom_boxplot(width = 0.6, outlier.size = 0.7, linewidth = 0.3) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(1, 6), breaks = 1:5) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = colors_iam) +
    labs(
      title = dim_name,
      x = "Condition",
      y = "Response (1 = low, 5 = high)"
    ) +
    theme_classic(base_size = 9) +
    theme(
      legend.position = "none",
      plot.title      = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5)
    )
  
  if (nrow(sig_dim) == 0)
    return(p)

  # Dynamische y-Positionen für Klammern
  y_base <- max(data_dim$Score, na.rm = TRUE) + 0.4
  y_step <- 0.4
  sig_dim$y_pos <- y_base + y_step * (seq_len(nrow(sig_dim)) - 1)
  
  ymax <- max(sig_dim$y_pos) + 0.4
  
  p +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(1, ymax), breaks = 1:5) +
    geom_signif(
      data       = sig_dim,
      manual     = TRUE,
      inherit.aes = FALSE,
      aes(
        xmin       = group1,
        xmax       = group2,
        annotations = stars,
        y_position = y_pos
      ),
      tip_length = 0.01,
      textsize   = 3
    )
}
```

1. compute success rate:

```{r}
dataPer$RGBD_Success <- 1 - dataPer$RGBD_Fails / 12
dataPer$PC_Success   <- 1 - dataPer$PC_Fails / 12
dataPer$RGBD_PC_Success <- 1 - dataPer$RGBD_PC_Fails / 12
dataPer$OT_Success <- 1 - dataPer$OT_Fails / 12
```

own: relative error
```{r}
dataPer$RGBD_RelFails <- dataPer$RGBD_Fails / 12
dataPer$PC_RelFails   <- dataPer$PC_Fails / 12
dataPer$RGBD_PC_RelFails <- dataPer$RGBD_PC_Fails / 12
dataPer$OT_RelFails   <- dataPer$OT_Fails / 12
```

Combined over 12 trials (4 trials for each task)


including error rates
```{r}
success_mat <- data.frame(
  RGBs    = dataPer$RGBD_Success,
  PC      = dataPer$PC_Success,
  PC_RGB  = dataPer$RGBD_PC_Success,
  OT      = dataPer$OT_Success
)

#means <- colMeans(success_mat, na.rm = TRUE)
#ses   <- apply(success_mat, 2, function(x) sd(x, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(sum(!is.na(x))))
```



```{r}
df <- success_mat %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = everything(),
               names_to = "Condition",
               values_to = "Success") %>%
  mutate(Condition = factor(Condition,
                            levels = c("RGBs", "PC", "PC_RGB", "OT")),
         Label = factor(Condition,
                        labels = c("RGBs", "PC", "PC+RGB", "OT")))

df_summary <- df %>%
  group_by(Condition, Label) %>%
  summarise(
    mean = mean(Success, na.rm = TRUE),
    se   = sd(Success, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n())
  )
```


```{r}
ggplot(df_summary, aes(x = Label, y = mean, fill = Label)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean - se, ymax = mean + se),
                width = 0.18, linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", mean),
                y = mean + se + 0.05),      # mehr Abstand!
            size = 5) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = colors_iam) +

  # Y-Achse leicht erweitern für Platz
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0.0, 1.1),
    breaks = seq(0.0, 1.0, by = 0.1),
    labels = sprintf("%.1f", seq(0.0, 1.0, 0.1))
  ) +

  labs(
    title = "Overall Success Rate by Condition",
    x = "",
    y = "Success Rate"
  ) +

  # Klare Achsenlinien (wie dein Vergleich)
  theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5)
  )

```

### significance testing

long format
```{r}
data_time_long <- dataPer %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(RGBD_mean, PC_mean, RGBD_PC_mean, OT_mean),
    names_to = "condition",
    values_to = "value"
  )

```

Pretest conditions
```{r}
# shapiro
data_time_long %>%
  group_by(condition) %>%
  shapiro_test(value)
```


```{r}
# levene
data_time_long %>% levene_test(value ~ condition)
```

friedman test
```{r}
friedman_res_time <- data_time_long %>%
  friedman_test(value ~ condition | id)

friedman_res_time

```


post-hoc tests
```{r}
posthoc_friedman_time <- data_time_long %>%
  pairwise_wilcox_test(
    value ~ condition, 
    paired = TRUE,
    p.adjust.method = "holm"
  )

posthoc_friedman_time
```



### Plot with significance results


```{r}

library(ggsignif) 


comp_long <- dataPer %>%
  select(id, RGBD_mean, PC_mean, RGBD_PC_mean, OT_mean) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols      = c(RGBD_mean, PC_mean, RGBD_PC_mean, OT_mean),
    names_to  = "Condition",
    values_to = "Time"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    id = factor(id),   # <-- wichtig
    Condition = factor(
      Condition,
      levels = c("RGBD_mean", "PC_mean", "RGBD_PC_mean", "OT_mean"),
      labels = c("RGBs", "PC", "PC+RGB", "OT")
    )
  )
```


```{r}
friedman_ct <- friedman_test(Time ~ Condition | id, data = comp_long)
friedman_ct

posthoc_ct <- comp_long %>%
  pairwise_wilcox_test(
    Time ~ Condition,
    paired = TRUE,
    p.adjust.method = "holm"
  )

posthoc_ct
```

```{r}
posthoc_ct2 <- posthoc_ct %>%
  mutate(
    signif3 = case_when(
      p.adj < 0.001 ~ "***",
      p.adj < 0.01  ~ "**",
      p.adj < 0.05  ~ "*",
      TRUE          ~ ""
    )
  )
```


```{r}
sig_pairs_ct <- posthoc_ct2 %>%
  filter(p.adj < 0.05) %>%
  transmute(
    group1,
    group2,
    stars = signif3    # <-- hier!
  )
```



```{r}
plot_completion_time <- function() {
  
  data_ct <- comp_long
  sig_ct  <- sig_pairs_ct
  
  p <- ggplot(
    data_ct,
    aes(x = Condition, y = Time, fill = Condition)
  ) +
    geom_boxplot(width = 0.6, outlier.size = 0.7, linewidth = 0.3) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = colors_iam) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 120), breaks = seq(0, 120, 20)) +
    labs(
      title = "Completion time",
      x     = "",
      y     = "Completion time in seconds"
    ) +
    theme_classic(base_size = 9) +
    theme(
      legend.position = "none",
      plot.title      = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5)
    )
  
  # falls nichts signifikant ist
  if (nrow(sig_ct) == 0)
    return(p)
  
  # Dynamische y-Positionen für die Klammern
  y_base <- max(data_ct$Time, na.rm = TRUE) + 5
  y_step <- 5
  sig_ct$y_pos <- y_base + y_step * (seq_len(nrow(sig_ct)) - 1)
  ymax <- max(sig_ct$y_pos) + 5
  
  p +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, ymax), breaks = seq(0, ymax, 20)) +
    geom_signif(
      data        = sig_ct,
      manual      = TRUE,
      inherit.aes = FALSE,
      aes(
        xmin        = group1,
        xmax        = group2,
        annotations = stars,
        y_position  = y_pos
      ),
      tip_length = 0.01,
      textsize   = 3
    )
}

p_ct <- plot_completion_time()
p_ct

```
